purpose: Ungraded, problem-first Android/Fire OS challenges. A topic is a navigational aid, not a mandatory prerequisite.

challenges.title: Why does a remote press sometimes trigger two actions?
challenges.problem: Observe actual KeyEvents and UI actions on Fire OS. Find when one physical gesture becomes multiple application actions, and design a minimally invasive interpretation that remains predictable.
tacit_checks: Capture a reproducible raw-versus-accepted input trace
Explain one duplicate-action failure using observed events
Change one normalization rule and compare the real result

challenges.title: What happens when Android interrupts an unfinished task?
challenges.problem: Build a tiny stateful interaction; switch to Home, force recreation and, when practical, process loss. Determine which state survives, which does not, and why.
tacit_checks: Distinguish view recreation from process death
Restore a visible in-progress state after recreation
challenges.local_start: Create a small independent app; never clear existing Console/browser data.

challenges.title: Can a game change its animation without rebuilding its engine?
challenges.problem: Load a tiny versioned external sprite bundle, then alter it independently of the game. Compare updates, cache reuse, version rollback and offline behavior.
tacit_checks: Update an asset independently of engine code
Show an unchanged cached asset is reused
Reopen with the previous verified asset when offline
challenges.local_start: Start with the native Playroom microgames as a rendering/control baseline; external loading remains unimplemented.

challenges.title: Can an iPad make a complex TV interface genuinely usable?
challenges.problem: Compare remote-only interaction with an optional iPad companion for a pointer/keyboard-intensive application. Observe latency, focus, reconnect and permission boundaries.
tacit_checks: Measure an end-to-end input round trip
Distinguish app-local input from system-wide injection
challenges.local_start: Treat TV-first control as the baseline; no background companion service exists yet.
